name: splunk-p2-foothold
title: Splunk Case 01, Part 2: from login to web shell

slides.kicker: case 01 · boss of the soc v1
slides.title: From batman to a working web shell in 7 minutes.
slides.sub: The admin session, two uploads and the first web shell request, traced in Splunk on the Boss of the SOC v1 practice dataset.

slides.title: 21:51:32: the browser opened eXtplorer
body: eXtplorer is a file manager in the Joomla admin area. The browser loaded it, then used it to list files and upload (slide 4). Only a logged-in admin can do that, so the batman login worked.
slides.caption: Filtered to the login IP and IE 11 (Trident). 3 min 27 s after the login.

slides.title: First try: agent.php through the Extension Installer
body: 21:50:31, a minute before eXtplorer. The server sent no success message, so this upload most likely failed.
slides.caption: This search found one upload. It did not show the one that worked.

slides.title: Second try at 21:52:47: Upload successful!
body: eXtplorer sent two files at once: agent.php and 3791.exe, a program that Part 3 follows. The firewall flagged 3791.exe during this upload and still let it through. That gets its own post.
slides.caption: I found this upload with a keyword search for 3791.exe, not with the part_filename search.

slides.cmd: agent.php | stats count by src_ip, http_method, uri_path, _time
slides.title: 21:55:22: the other IP starts using agent.php
body: 23.22.63[.]114, the IP that ran the brute force, sends GET requests to the web shell, a few per second.
slides.caption: One attacker, two IPs: one uploaded the shell, the other used it.

slides.title: Plain GET requests, commands in the headers
bullets: The URL is only /joomla/agent.php. The commands travel in the Referer and Accept-Language headers.
In one request (22:21:34): a fake Google Referer, a fake Safari User-Agent and a strange Accept-Language, `it-CH,pa;q=0.5,ps;q=0.7,pa;q=0.8`.
The reply is encoded, between tags that match a key in the agent.php code.
So the URL alone shows no command. The headers do.

slides.title: Login to web shell: 7 min 17 s
bullets: 21:50:31 first agent.php upload, Extension Installer (most likely failed)

slides.title: Cheat sheet: login to shell
bullets: Did the login work? See the next requests: `sourcetype=stream:http src_ip=<ip> | table _time http_method uri_path status | sort _time`
Uploads with a file name (it missed one): `sourcetype=stream:http http_method=POST part_filename=* | table _time src_ip part_filename`
One file in web, firewall, IDS: `<file> sourcetype IN ("stream:http", "fgt_utm", "suricata") | sort _time`
A field search misses events with empty fields. Also search the plain file name.

body: What agent.php ran on the server, the reverse shell, and how the website's image was replaced.
